reviews.text: Elite soundtrack, great CGI, alien robots, it’s peak. Been way too long since I revisited this, and I meant to when Cullen passed but totally forgot. I do think this slightly drags, and could’ve cut a good 20 minutes that would’ve helped a lot. It introduces everything well and has great humor with Sam, although LaBeouf is a very questionable person now. It’s just such a fun, action-filled watch, and although it has its flaws, it’s hard not to love it. Some of the government scenes are hilarious now that I can actually understand the satire, considering my last watch was at least 6 years ago. RIP Peter Cullen

"I am Optimus Prime, and I send this message to any surviving Autobots taking refuge among the stars. We are here. We are waiting". Desde su creación Optimus Prime en toda adaptación, su liderazgo se basa en la responsabilidad, la empatía y la protección de aquellos que no pueden defenderse por sí mismos, Optimus ni siquiera busca el gobernar, sino preservar la libertad incluso en medio de una guerra. En contraste, Megatron encarna una búsqueda de poder que transforma el conflicto en una lucha cada vez más destructiva. Los humanos, por otro lado, constantemente intentan comprender, controlar o utilizar aquello que desconocen, especialmente cuando perciben una posible ventaja militar. Esta diferencia plantea una crítica interesante: una civilización tecnológicamente avanzada no necesariamente es una civilización moralmente superior. Aunque su guión puede resultar sencillo, la película consigue transmitir una sensación constante de caos, velocidad y capacidad de asombrarte por los efectos especiales.

An engaging blockbuster overall, but definitely one that loses itself its the final act. Starting off with its thrilling political intrigue, espionage, and military action, Transformers hooks you from the start with its brisk pace. LaBeouf is brilliant as Sam, flawlessly conveying his nerdy and comedic traits. The CGI’s thoroughly impressive, though they lack the holistic perspective of later films (not exactly a flaw). The character designs are brilliant (save perhaps Megatron), with the original lineup of Autobots and Decepticons being highly distinct from their respective groups. The action is fun for the most part, but certainly not as innovative or prominent as in later instalments. While Bumblebee received a major focus, I certainly wish Optimus had more screen time. Unfortunately, flaws are prevalent in the film’s middle and final acts. The Autobots hiding outside Sam’s home is cute at first, but quickly becomes obnoxious. The initial sequences with Sector 7 are largely uninteresting, hindering the previously thrilling pace. As for the final act, action sequences with the actual Transformers are brief. The overall resolution is abrupt, with Megatron feeling dumbed down for the sake of it. Still iconic, but lacks the action the Bayverse is known for. I don’t know how, but the military propaganda in Bay’s initial trilogy just works. And that ending scene is just legendary
Besides the Dorito shaped Starscream, spiky metal Megatron, and Micheal Bay’s weird fetishes and somewhat messy writing, it’s still pretty cool and a solid movie.

It’s been nearly 20 years since Transformers first released in theatres and I would still say that this is some of the best CGI to ever grace our screens. It’s honestly a cinematic feat. The movie has its own issues, like the hypersexualization of the female teenage lead, but I was honestly impressed at how well it held up upon rewatch. The sound design is incredible and makes every fight sequence feel so epic. Flawless pacing that takes its time to introduce vital characters instead of dropping you right into the action. The score and soundtrack is just so fantastic and so much fun. The final monologue playing out into Linkin Park’s “What I’ve Done”? Cinema!

Absolutely a propaganda movie about the US military, but it’s so worth the watch. Transformers (2007) is one of those movies that the whole family can enjoy. Action, comedy, romance, it has everything. Shia LaBeouf has a career defining performance as Sam. He’s smart, funny, and logical. At first it seems he’s a basic nerd who wants the girl, but he is shown to be witty and sincere. In the ocean of solid performances, there are a few that reach his watchability. Omar Benson Miller bashing through the glass window and getting tackled into the pool. Anthony Anderson and the donuts. Josh Duhamel as a stereotypical but affable soldier. Kevin Dunn and Julie White as probably the most enjoyable movie parents I’ve ever seen. And of course, Peter Cullen (rip) as the infamous Optimus Prime. This movie lays a foundation of a trilogy that would rock the late 2000’s family living room. Also, for me, this put Linkin Park on the map of everyone else who wasn’t already fans of the band. Michael Bay nails this movie in the most Michael Bay way.

In memory of Peter Cullen, I've decided to watch and complete this movie finally. What a solid fun action movie. It's silly, it's fun, it's hype, it's peak. The simple story of the Autobots protecting the cube while the Decepticons try to retrieve it is compelling enough and it works for this movie. The protagonist, Sam, is a flawed but fun protagonist who ends up saving the day in the end cause like it's aura and he becomes a true hero, which was great to see. Megan Fox as Mikaela was great as well, the chemistry between her and our protagonist worked well especially standing out in the first half of the movie. The military guys were cool too, there was one part where one of the guys genuinely risked his life for the clip I loved it. And of course the Transformers themselves were great, showing each of their personalities in a simple but effective way. The Transformers looked great especially for 2007 standards and of course they had tons of hype moments and aura. Optimus with his speeches, Megatron with his aura one liners, Bumblebee with his playfulness and the rest of them with their guns and ammo. During the action scenes in this film, you can genuinely turn your brain off and let your eyes enjoy while during the other scenes, the simple yet effective story progression and comedy is fulfilling. So yeah overall great movie and RIP Peter Cullen, he'll forever be the hopeful, good hearted Optimus Prime... (Music builds up) WHATTTTT I'VE DONEEEE Directed by Michael Bay
